name: La Fortuna Town
tagline: The central park and the main street, with Arenal behind it
description: The town itself, a grid of streets around a church and a small park with the volcano rising directly behind, holding the tour agencies, the restaurants, the supermarkets and the bus terminal. It is the only place here where you can live without a vehicle.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the shops, the agencies and the buses on foot
pros: All tour operators, banks and supermarkets close by
The volcano framed at the end of the street
cons: The highest rents in the area
Tourist pricing on food and services
Tour vans and traffic through the centre

name: El Castillo
tagline: The village on the lake shore, under the volcano's south side
description: A small settlement on the road along Lake Arenal beneath the volcano's southern flank, with rainforest, hanging bridges and the best direct views of the cone. It is quiet, spread out and considerably more remote than the town, with a rough road connecting them.
bestFor: Stays that want the volcano view and the forest rather than a town
pros: The best uninterrupted views of Arenal
Rainforest, hanging bridges and wildlife at the door
cons: Forty minutes on a rough road into town
A four-wheel-drive vehicle is close to necessary

name: Tabacon and the Hot Springs Road
tagline: The thermal river road northwest of town
description: The stretch of highway running northwest towards the lake where the thermal rivers surface and the major hot spring resorts have built, from the free public river crossing to the large landscaped complexes. Accommodation is mostly hotels and lodges rather than long-term rentals.
bestFor: Short stays built around the hot springs and the volcano trails
pros: Thermal rivers and the major hot spring resorts
Closest to the national park entrance
Rainforest on both sides of the road
cons: Fifteen minutes into town and a vehicle is needed

name: Z-13 and the Southern Barrios
tagline: The residential streets where the town actually lives
description: The residential neighbourhoods spreading south and east from the centre, where the people who work in La Fortuna's tourism industry live, with ordinary houses, local sodas and small shops. Rents are a fraction of anything tourist-facing and the centre is a ten-minute walk.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting local prices and a normal neighbourhood
pros: Rents well below the tourist areas
Local sodas and shops at Costa Rican prices
Ten minutes on foot to the centre
cons: No tourist services or English nearby

name: Lake Arenal Shore (25 km west)
tagline: Along the reservoir towards Nuevo Arenal
description: The road running west along the shore of the artificial lake towards Nuevo Arenal, with scattered houses and lodges on the hillsides above the water, wind for kitesurfing at the western end, and a small foreign resident community that has been there for decades.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting lake views, wind sports and an established foreign community
pros: Lake views and reliable wind for kitesurfing
Much lower rents than La Fortuna
cons: Forty-five minutes to an hour into La Fortuna
Very limited services and wet, windy weather
